newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soycomplex exports continue slide in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soycomplex exports continue slide in Sept.

text.p: Brazilian soycomplex shipments fell in September from August, continuing a slowdown in exports seen in recent months, inspection company SGS do Brasil said.
Soybean exports in September dropped 8.6 percent to 257,900 tonnes, soymeal by 12.6 percent to 828,900 tonnes and soyoil 25.2 percent to 119,600 tonnes, it added in a statement.
The fall was also reflected in the nine-month period between January to September 1996 compared with the corresponding period in 1995, with soybeans down 6.7 percent and soyoil 11.4 percent.
Only soymeal showed a positive increase, rising 6.1 percent in the first nine months of this year to 8.54 million tonnes.
Shipments from the port of Paranagua in the first nine months of 1996 were 5.01 million tonnes of soymeal, 1.87 million tonnes of soybeans and 627,100 tonnes of soyoil.
Other sizeable shipments were made from the port of Rio Grande totalling 1.91 million tonnes soymeal and 251,400 soybeans, SGS do Brasil said.
Of the January to September total shipped from Paranagua, 59,000 tonnes of soybeans and 75,600 tonnes of soymeal were from Paraguay.
Other exports from Paraguay were made through Santos (115,100 tonnes of soybeans and 26,500 tonnes of soymeal in January to September) and 110,100 tonnes of soybeans from Rio Grande.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
